item.title: Financial conditions are the easiest since 1997, and 2.4 million people walked out of the labour market
item.dc:creator: The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter)
item.description: The US Index of Financial Conditions has climbed to 1.29 points, the easiest reading since 1997. Borrowing and deploying money has not been this cheap in three decades. Yet the labour and household numbers released the same week pointed the other way. item.dc:creator: The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter)
item.description: America's job-openings figure is built from the roughly one in four businesses that agree to answer, the source says. Before the pandemic, the source says, that share ran between half and seven in ten. Reporting on the same trend uses a slightly different yardstick. item.title: Half the copper left in London's warehouses already has an owner waiting
item.dc:creator: The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter)
item.description: About half of the copper still sitting in London Metal Exchange warehouses has already been claimed for withdrawal. Stockpiles have fallen for 42 straight trading days, and over that stretch anyone who needs metal today has ended up paying far more than someone willing to wait a month. item.description: The expectation that the European Central Bank will buy your government bonds comes with conditions that are written down. item.description: The oil the United States keeps buried for emergencies is down to 298.7 million barrels. It has not been below 300 million since January 1983.
